root.name: Grünfeld Defense: Brinckmann Attack
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 d5 4. Bf4

overview: White develops the bishop to f4 before Black has committed, a London-style anti-Grünfeld approach. After 4...Bg7 5.e3 O-O Black strikes the centre with ...c5 or ...dxc4, or accepts the cxd5 Nxd5 exchanges. White keeps a solid structure and flexible development; Black has comfortable counterplay. The play is positional and less theoretical than the main Grünfeld lines.

white_ideas.idea: Build a solid centre with e3, Nf3 and Be2 or Rc1
Meet ...c5 with dxc5 or Nf3 and keep the pieces active
Avoid main-line Grünfeld theory with a London-style set-up

black_ideas.idea: Put pressure on d4 with ...Bg7 and ...Nc6 or ...Be6
Let White build the centre and attack it with pieces

typical_structures.structure: Grünfeld centre with Black d5/c5 pressure against White's d4 and e3

character.notes: Quiet, positional White set-up; Black has comfortable counterplay.

gambit.notes: No material offered; cxd5 Nxd5 exchanges.

structure.notes: Centre in tension with exchanges possible.

approach.notes: A named line used occasionally by strong players.

level.notes: Plans are straightforward; little forcing theory.
